What Apple Reduce Loud Sounds is — and what your listing may claim

Apple ships Reduce Loud Sounds under Settings → Sounds & Haptics → Headphone Safety → Reduce Loud Sounds. When enabled, the device limits maximum headphone output volume to help protect hearing. Western indie listings often show one or more of these surfaces on the US product page. AppLocale covers paste-ready zh-Hans copy for whichever your screenshots and description already claim:

  • Reduce Loud Sounds toggle (降低高音量) — master switch that caps maximum headphone volume. Gallery frames may show the Headphone Safety settings branch or a "Works with Reduce Loud Sounds" badge.
  • Maximum headphone volume cap (耳机音量上限) — marketing that emphasizes a ceiling on headphone output level. Screenshot overlays often show volume sliders capped at a safe maximum, Headphone Safety settings walkthroughs, or before/after volume-limit comparisons.
  • Headphone safety volume limit (音量限制) — when your English listing explains that users cannot push headphone volume past a hearing-health threshold. zh-Hans copy should use 音量限制 and 耳机安全 only when your US page already claims Headphone Safety framing — not as a generic medical guarantee.
  • Safe-listening volume workflows in your app — in-app audio players, podcast episodes, kids modes, or parental dashboards that respect or complement system Reduce Loud Sounds when loud content plays. Screenshot overlays often show volume-cap badges on player UI or Headphone Safety settings walkthroughs.

Your gallery may lead with a Reduce Loud Sounds toggle on one frame and an in-app volume ceiling on the next. zh-Hans caption lines should name the correct surface per frame — a volume-cap toggle is not a Headphone Notifications exposure alert banner, not an Environmental Sound Levels dB readout, and not a Noise Notifications ambient noise card unless that is what the screenshot shows. Headphone Safety is the parent Settings pane that also contains Headphone Notifications — mention Headphone Safety only as the parent path; this SKU covers the Reduce Loud Sounds volume-cap toggle only.
